item.title: Nahigatoka rallies behind Nadroga ahead of do-or-die Skipper Cup clash at 3pm

item.content:encoded:
Nahigatoka Village has rallied behind the Nadroga Stallions ahead of the crucial do-or-die stage of the 2026 Skipper Cup, bringing together current players and rugby legends to reaffirm the village’s generations-long support for Nadroga Rugby.

The gathering brought together current players and former Nadroga rugby legends who hail from Nahigatoka, with the occasion reflecting the strong historical connection between the village and the provincial side.

The Nadroga Rugby Legends say the gathering brought back memories of the Golden Era of Nadroga Rugby, when the Stallions dominated the local rugby scene and collected numerous titles.

They say Nahigatoka played an important role during that era, with former players from the village returning this week to stand alongside the current generation of Stallions.

The Legends say while the players and generations have changed, the support and passion for Nadroga Rugby remain strong.

They say the current players should remember that the Nadroga jersey represents history, sacrifice, family and the villages and people who have supported the provincial side through generations.

The occasion also highlighted the contribution of three influential Nadroga coaches from Nahigatoka Village who led the Stallions during different periods of the team's Golden Era.

Vilikesa Bola coached during the 1960s, Adriu Nadredre during the 1970s, while Ratu Meli Kurisaru's era stretched from the 1980s to the early 2000s.

The Nadroga Rugby Legends say the three coaches helped mould players, develop talent and instil discipline in teams that went on to dominate the local rugby scene.

They say as leadership passed from one coach to another, the knowledge, experience, discipline and passion associated with Nadroga Rugby were also passed on to the next generation.

The Legends thanked the people of Nahigatoka Village for their hospitality, generosity and continued support for the Stallions.

They say the gathering was about more than providing the players with a meal, as it reminded the team that thousands of people continue to believe in and support them.

The current Stallions have also been urged to remember the coaches, players and communities that came before them as they head into the crucial stage of their Skipper Cup campaign.

The Nadroga Rugby Legends say it is now up to the current generation to carry the legacy forward and write their own chapter in the proud history of Nadroga Rugby.

In Round Six of the Skipper Cup today, Nadroga will take on Ba at Lawaqa Park.

In other matches, Taveuni will face Naitasiri at Ratu Cakobau Park, Tailevu will take on Rewa at Nakelo District School, Nadi will face Navosa at King Charles Park, Lautoka will take on Malolo at Churchill Park, while Kadavu will face Suva at Nasese.

item.title: Marama Championship set for epic Round 6 showdown
item.description: An epic round of competition is expected in the Subrails Marama Championship today, with teams set to battle it out across six fixtures in Round 6. item.content:encoded:
An epic round of competition is expected in the Subrails Marama Championship today, with teams set to battle it out across six fixtures in Round 6.

Lautoka will face Namosi at Churchill Park in Lautoka at 11am, while Nadroga will take on Ba at Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka at the same time.

At Nasese, Kadavu will go up against Suva at 1pm in what is expected to be another competitive encounter.

Tailevu will face Rewa at Nakelo School Ground at 11am, while Nadi will host Nasinu at Prince Charles Park at 11am, while Naitasiri take on Macuata at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori at 11am.

item.title: Taveuni Rugby team receives major boost from diaspora in America
item.description: Taveuni Rugby received a much-needed boost to their Skipper Cup campaign following the donation of more than $14,000 from the Fijian diaspora living in the United States. The total donation of $14,698.49 reflects the continued commitment of Fijians living abroad in supporting grassroots rugby.
item.content:encoded:
Taveuni Rugby received a much-needed boost to their Skipper Cup campaign following the donation of more than $14,000 from the Fijian diaspora living in the United States.

The total donation of $14,698.49 reflects the continued commitment of Fijians living abroad in supporting grassroots rugby.

The Taveuni Management says $12,698.49 was allocated to player allowances last night , helping the squad with their final preparations ahead of tomorrow’s crucial clash.

They say the support has gone far beyond financial contributions and the Taveuni community in America has stepped in at critical moment throughout the team’s journey away from home, including assistance with transportation costs.

The management says their contributions have included transportation for DiMila’s reguregu and Qasina Loa in Naduri, as well as transport from Lautoka to Suva, with a total of $2,000 committed towards transportation.

Taveuni is expecting a physical encounter when they take on Naitasiri at 3pm tomorrow at Ratu Cakobau Park in Nausori.

In other matches, Tailevu will take on Rewa at Nakelo District School Ground, while Nadi faces Navosa at King Charles Park.

In Lautoka, the home side will meet Malolo, while Nadroga takes on Ba at Lawaqa Park.

item.title: Fijiana XV hold off Japan to secure 15-12 victory
item.description: The Vodafone Fijiana XV held off a determined Japan side to secure a hard-fought 15-12 victory in their international Test match last night. Fiji made a strong start with fullback Ivamere Rokowati crossing for the opening try in the 8th minute to give the Fijiana a 5-0 lead.
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fijiana XV held off a determined Japan side to secure a hard-fought 15-12 victory in their international Test match last night.

Fiji made a strong start with fullback Ivamere Rokowati crossing for the opening try in the 8th minute to give the Fijiana a 5-0 lead.

Varanisese Qoro extended Fiji's advantage with their second try in the 20th minute as the Fijiana went 10-0 ahead.

Japan responded in the 27th minute through Nami Asari, with Maiko Nishi adding the conversion to reduce Fiji's lead to 10-7.

The Vodafone Fijiana XV maintained their three-point advantage heading into half-time.

Fiji struck again early in the second half when winger Aqela Raitubu crossed in the 50th minute to extend their lead to 15-7.

Japan refused to go away and hit back through Asuka Kuge in the 56th minute to close the gap to 15-12.

Despite Japan applying pressure in the latter stages of the match, the Fijiana defence held firm as neither side managed to add further points before the final whistle.

Fiji dominated the attacking territory during the match, making 17 entries into Japan's 22 compared with six by the hosts.

The Fijiana also won 116 rucks compared with Japan's 79 and spent 74 minutes in the lead.

The 15-12 victory gives the Vodafone Fijiana XV a winning start to their Japan Rugby Challenge Match campaign at JAPAN BASE in Fukuoka.
